p2 Case 1 verbatim. The source also speculates that concurrent upper-body strength and endurance work during lower-body restriction predisposed six of seven pec major injuries (p4), which the claim does not capture.

statementIssues.note: 'Avoid compensating with unplanned overload in the unrestricted body region' is advice not stated in C17; the source's own speculation (concurrent upper-body endurance/strength work, biweekly PR bench attempts) could support a version of it but was not claimed. Should be labeled professional caution or backed by a claim.
Says several sources are legacy records without full-text review, but every source is marked fullTextReviewed true; also lists 9 sources while 10 are cited (484 is a third single-team study).
'This shows who needs top-up exposure and who needs recovery' is an inference beyond C10/C11, which describe a load gap and a recommendation for limited-minute players only.
Congestion evidence uses 2+ matches within 4 days or less recovery; applying it to a single-competition week with travel is a transfer the brief does not flag.

tierNote: Limited is appropriate: indirect, mostly observational male professional soccer evidence with genuine tension on MD-2 speed placement, and major parts of the question (strength allocation, travel, readiness criteria, modified participation) uncovered. recommendedDirection is null and actions are framed as options, as the gating requires.
usefulnessNote: Clearly lays out the D-2 versus mid-week speed choice, the starter/non-starter gap and the absence of a validated readiness rule, and is honest that strength, travel and modified-participation planning are gaps. A practitioner gets a framing for one field session but little concrete help for the full seven-day allocation asked about.
suggestedDrafterFixes: Keep tier dimensions consistent with the sources array: derive the full-text-review statement and the source-type counts from the cited sources rather than free text.
When a guardrail or action adds advice not stated in its cited claims, either add a claim that supports it or label it explicitly as professional caution.
When a claim's source gives concrete specifics that bear on the decision (e.g. which days to adjust and why), include them in the claim rather than truncating to the general statement.
Name the exposure definition of a source (e.g. congestion = 2+ matches within 4 days) when the request's schedule differs from it.
